pr_title: drivers: udc_nrf: Do not submit buffer more than once
pr_body:
When the UDC buffer gets submitted it should no longer reside in the endpoint queue. While this commit does not address the underlying issue of not being able to start transfer for whatever reason, it prevents the problem from cascading into buffer double completion (e.g. receive buffer double free in UAC2).

Fix: #84664

issue_context.title: USB: device_next: `buf_release_cb` may be called with `NULL` buffer
issue_context.body:
Rarely, when `usbd_uac2_send` is called, the `uac2_ops.buf_release_cb` may be called an additional time with the buffer set to `NULL`. If an application implements the callback like 

```c
static void uac2_buf_release_cb(const struct device *dev, uint8_t terminal, void *buf,
				void *user_data)
{
	k_mem_slab_free(&usb_out_buf_pool, buf);
}
```

Then this will fail as calling `k_mem_slab_free` with `NULL` is invalid behavior. The callback is not described as ever giving a `NULL` buffer, but what is more odd is that it is called an additional time with NULL. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Build and flash the sample from https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/84359 for `nrf5340_audio_dk/nrf5340/cpuapp` with `CONFIG_ASSERT=y`
2. Build and flash the sample from https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/84553 for `nrf5340_audio_dk/nrf5340/cpuapp`
3. See error (usually in the first few seconds). 

Step 1 can alternatively also be done on the nRF52840DK, and built as 
```
west build -b nrf52840dk/nrf52840 -- -DEXTRA_CONF_FILE=overlay-bt_ll_sw_split.conf -DCONFIG_ASSERT=y
```

**Expected behavior**
Expect `uac2_ops.buf_release_cb` to never be called with `NULL`, or that is documented to happened for some reason. 

**Impact**
Easy workaround is to add checks in the application for `NULL`

**Logs and console output**
`uac2_sof_cb` logs the address of the buffer before calling `usbd_uac2_send` and `uac2_buf_release_cb` logs the address of the buffer from the callback arguments. 

It can be seen that `uac2_sof_cb` calls `usbd_uac2_send` 2 times, but `uac2_buf_release_cb` is called 3 times; 2 times with the expected buffer addresses and once with `0`/`NULL`.

It seems to only happen in the beginning of the stream. Unsure if the amount of logging hogs the CPU and makes it worse or not.

This is bug in nRF UDC driver, caused because:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/77a350efa74ef6795d056392cb5001b917ff4f69/drivers/usb/udc/udc_nrf.c#L118-L119

submits the buffer to the stack but does not remove it from the queue. Then the very same buffer gets submitted again, but because the `net_buf` gets freed on its first handling, the `__buf` is NULL.

review_comments: As noted in the comment above, remove the buffer from the endpoint queue and return it to the stack. Do not remove `udc_submit_ep_event(dev, buf, -ECONNREFUSED);`. The same goes for the line below.

The problem is that this code path happens because there is no proper synchronization between the udc nrf thread processing posted messages to the queue and the rest of the USB stack. The buffer is in fact used by the DMA when this problem happens and hence the quick solution, before the proper synchronization is implemented is to avoid submitting the buffer more than one.
